fields.Trigger: Customer purchases warranty-eligible product at POS or online

Automation Opportunity: - Warranty-eligible auto-detected from the item master; serial auto-validated; vendor-push auto-retried on failure
Controls: - CTL-194 (ensure warranty registration & claim integrity.); CTL-388 (ensure controlled execution — Product Warranty Registration & Activation (PA-53.1).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Serial-capture-skipped risk**: the cashier skips the serial-number capture (rushed checkout), making a future claim untraceable to the specific unit; mitigated by the mandatory-serial-field for serial-numbered SKUs (the POS won't proceed without it)

- **Vendor-API-failure risk**: the registration push to the vendor portal fails silently, so the vendor doesn't know about the warranty; mitigated by the W2123 data-quality audit catching the push failure
System Touchpoints: - POS / warranty capture (links to VS-08 / W5B, POS-013 real-time) — the warranty-eligible identification and capture
- CRM warranty module (links to VS-13 / W17, W156 CDP) — the warranty record
- Vendor portal (links to VS-28 / W593) — the vendor registration push
Time Estimate: ~90 sec/transaction × ~420,000/month = **~10,500 hours/month Cashier** (absorbed into checkout, ~15 sec incremental over a normal scan).

steps.activity: POS auto-identifies warranty-eligible SKU at scan; prompts cashier; captures transaction date, SKU, serial number, store, loyalty ID; generates warranty record in CRM
Cashier prints warranty card with terms, duration, claim instructions, and registration QR code; customer scans for digital warranty wallet
For serial-numbered items: cashier scans or enters serial number; system validates format and links to item+transaction record
System pushes registration to vendor portal (real-time for top 20 vendors; batch daily for others); customer receives SMS/email confirmation

fields.Trigger: Ecommerce order with warranty-eligible items fulfilled

Automation Opportunity: - Registration auto-generated on fulfillment; serial-reminders auto-sent; vendor-push auto-retried
Controls: - CTL-37: warranty validity; CTL-44 (registration integrity); operational: Ecommerce Ops monitoring
Pain Points / Risks: - **Serial-registration-non-completion risk**: the customer doesn't register the serial within 14 days (they forget), making the warranty unclaimable; mitigated by the day-7 and day-13 reminders and the 14-day grace extension

- **Fulfillment-trigger-timing risk**: the warranty start-date is the fulfillment confirmation (not the order date), but the customer may expect it from the order date; mitigated by the warranty-start-date clearly stated on the certificate
System Touchpoints: - Ecommerce / warranty (links to VS-10 / W11, W98 order) — the auto-registration on fulfillment
- CRM (links to VS-13 / W17) — the warranty record linked to the customer profile
- Vendor portal (links to VS-28 / W593) — the vendor push
Time Estimate: Automated; Ecommerce Ops ~2 hours/week monitoring = **~100 hours/year**.

steps.activity: Ecommerce platform identifies warranty-eligible SKUs; auto-generates registration upon fulfillment confirmation; sends digital warranty certificate via email
For serial-numbered items: customer prompted to register serial via online form within 14 days; system sends reminders at day 7 and 13
Warranty data pushed to vendor portal; record linked to customer profile in CRM and visible in mobile app

fields.Participants: Head of Trade / Account Management, Customer
fields.Trigger: Trade/corporate account purchases warranty items in bulk

workflows.name: Bulk Warranty Registration for Trade Accounts

Automation Opportunity: - Project warranty auto-created from the trade invoice; per-item registration auto-generated; expiry-alerts auto-scheduled
Controls: - CTL-37: warranty validity; CTL-06 (project/customer master); operational: Head of Trade / Account Management sign-off on project warranty files
Pain Points / Risks: - **Phase-start-date-misalignment risk**: the warranty starts on the invoice date but the item is delivered months later (phased), shortening the effective coverage; mitigated by the project-level start-date tied to delivery confirmation (not invoice date)
- **Bulk-item-individual-tracking risk**: a 100-item bulk warranty is registered as a block, losing individual-item traceability; mitigated by the per-item registration within the project file
System Touchpoints: - CRM / project warranty (links to VS-13 / W17, VS-11 / W58 corporate account) — the project-level warranty file
- Phased-delivery integration (links to VS-11 / W164 staged delivery, VS-77 material staging) — the per-phase start-date
- Vendor portal (links to VS-28 / W593) — the vendor registration
Time Estimate: ~25 min/bulk × ~1,050/month = **~440 hours/month Trade Account Manager** (distributed across the trade team).

steps.activity: Account Manager creates project warranty file in CRM: links all items to project ID, customer account, delivery addresses
System auto-registers each item with project-level warranty start date (may differ from invoice date for phased deliveries)
Account Manager sends consolidated warranty schedule to customer; system schedules expiry alerts at 30 and 90 days before expiry

fields.Trigger: Homeowner requests warranty transfer to new property owner

Automation Opportunity: - Transfer auto-processed on CSR verification; vendor-notification auto-sent
Controls: - CTL-37: warranty validity; CTL-153 (consented identity-verification data — links to VS-91 / W53); operational: CS Director sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fraudulent-transfer risk**: a non-owner requests a transfer to access warranty coverage on items they didn't purchase; mitigated by the original-purchase verification (proof of purchase, identity)

- **Partial-transfer-ambiguity risk**: some items transfer and some don't (the new owner bought some, the old kept some), creating confusion; mitigated by the item-level transfer (not a blanket property transfer)
System Touchpoints: - CRM warranty (links to VS-13 / W17) — the original-purchase verification and the transfer record
- Vendor portal (links to VS-28 / W593) — the vendor-notification of the transfer
- Extended warranty (links to VS-53 / W2134) — the renewal offer on expired items

steps.activity: CSR verifies original purchase in CRM; confirms warranty status, remaining coverage; creates transfer record with new owner details
System sends transfer confirmation to both parties; updates vendor portal; notes expired items and offers extended warranty renewal

fields.Participants: Category Manager, VP Merchandising, IT, Legal
fields.Trigger: New product category or warranty terms change

Automation Opportunity: - Warranty config auto-pushed from the item master to POS/ecom; RA 7394-compliance auto-checked
Controls: - CTL-51: warranty-master data quality; warranty terms conform to the Consumer Act (RA 7394) — links to VS-22; operational: VP Merchandising sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **RA 7394-non-compliance risk**: the warranty terms don't meet the Consumer Act's minimum (e.g., implied warranty on the sale), creating a consumer-protection exposure; mitigated by the Legal review in step 2
- **Config-vs-master-desync risk**: the warranty master says one duration but the POS prompt says another (config drift); mitigated by the single-source master and the config-refresh
System Touchpoints: - Item/warranty master (links to VS-29 / W252, W296 service-item master) — the warranty parameters per SKU
- POS/ecom config (links to VS-08 / POS, VS-10) — the warranty-prompt and serial-capture rules
- Legal/compliance (links to VS-22 / W22.1 regulatory, VS-88) — the RA 7394 warranty-disclosure review
Time Estimate: ~2 hours/change × ~7/month = **~14 hours/month** Category Manager + IT + Legal.

steps.activity: Category Manager defines warranty parameters: type, duration, coverage scope, claim process; Merch Planner configures in ERP item master
IT configures POS/ecommerce prompts and serial capture rules; Legal reviews for Consumer Act (RA 7394) compliance

Controls: - CTL-388 (ensure controlled execution — Product Warranty Registration & Activation (PA-53.1).)
- operational: warranty-data quality; warranty validity — the audit ensures claims are valid; operational: VP Merchandising monthly sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Silent-data-decay risk**: warranty records accumulate quality issues (missing serials, orphaned contacts) without detection, undermining claim validity; mitigated by the monthly audit
- **Root-cause-neglect risk**: quality issues are corrected one-by-one without fixing the systemic cause (a POS config error); mitigated by the root-cause analysis and the system-fix
System Touchpoints: - Data quality (links to VS-29 / W291 master-data-quality monitoring) — the warranty-record quality checks
- CRM (links to VS-13 / W17) — the warranty records audited
- Vendor portal (links to VS-28 / W593) — the vendor-push failure check

steps.activity: System generates quality report: registrations without serials, without contacts, duplicates, date anomalies
Analyst spot-checks 500 records; identifies root causes; escalates training gaps, config errors, or vendor API failures

fields.Trigger: Customer accesses warranty portal via app/web

Automation Opportunity: - Wallet auto-populated from the CRM; alerts auto-sent; claim-initiation auto-routed
Controls: - CTL-388: data-privacy handling — links to VS-91 / W53; CTL-37 (warranty validity in the portal); operational: Digital PM adoption review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Adoption-low risk**: customers don't activate the digital wallet, so the proactive alerts and self-service claim don't reach them; mitigated by the QR-code at checkout (W2118) and the activation incentive
- **Data-privacy risk**: the portal shows purchase history and product details; mitigated by the RA 10173 consent and authentication per VS-91 / W53
System Touchpoints: - App/web portal (links to VS-75 / digital engagement, VS-10 / W98) — the warranty wallet surface
- CRM (links to VS-13 / W17, W156 CDP) — the warranty data source
- Push notifications (links to VS-75 app) — the proactive alerts

steps.activity: Customer logs in; sees all warranties by status (active, expiring, expired); can view details, claim history, remaining coverage
System proactively alerts: warranty expiring in 90 days, product recall notifications, seasonal maintenance reminders
Customer can initiate claim from portal; upload photos; track status in real-time with push notifications

Automation Opportunity: - Dashboard auto-refreshed; high-claim-rate auto-flagged; weekly operational metrics auto-distributed
Controls: - CTL-388 (ensure controlled execution — Product Warranty Registration & Activation (PA-53.1).)
- CTL-388: warranty-program register accuracy; operational: VP Merchandising monthly sign-off; Category Manager review on >5% claim rate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Claim-rate-spike-blindness risk**: a category's claim rate spikes (a quality issue) but isn't caught until month-end; mitigated by the weekly operational metrics alongside the monthly dashboard
- **Cost-vs-customer-experience-imbalance risk**: pushing the warranty-cost % down (denying more claims) erodes customer satisfaction; mitigated by the satisfaction KPI alongside the cost KPI
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113) — the warranty-program dashboard
- CRM/warranty (links to VS-13 / W17, VS-53 / W2118–W2133) — the warranty dataset
- P&L (links to VS-17 / W9, VS-158 / W85) — the warranty-cost view
Time Estimate: ~2.5 hours/month = **~30 hours/year** VP Merchandising + Category Managers.

steps.activity: System generates dashboard: active warranties by category, registration rate, claim rate, avg resolution time, warranty cost %, extended warranty attach rate
Category Managers review high claim rate categories (>5%); CS Director reviews claim satisfaction (target ≥80%); VP reviews warranty P&L
